sections.h2: What is Cass County, North Dakota?
sections.html:
Cass County is the most populous county in North Dakota, on the state's eastern edge along the Red River, and Fargo is its seat and largest city. The Dakota Territory legislature defined it on January 4, 1873, and it was organized on October 27 of that year. It is named for George Washington Cass, president of the Northern Pacific Railway from 1872 to 1875.

The county covers 1,767.8 square miles, almost all of it land. The Red River flows north along the eastern boundary with Minnesota. The terrain is low rolling hills, mostly farmed except around developed areas, sloping to the north and east, with the highest point at 1,194 feet in the southwest corner. The 2020 census counted 184,525 residents and the 2025 estimate is 201,794, about a quarter of the state's population.

The county is part of the Fargo-Moorhead metropolitan area. Interstates 29 and 94 cross it, along with US 10, 52 and 81, and Amtrak's Empire Builder stops in Fargo. MATBUS runs local transit.

sections.h2: Which cities and school districts are in Cass County?
sections.html:
Cass County has 27 incorporated cities, and your city and school district decide which mill levy applies to your house. The list includes Fargo, West Fargo, Casselton, Kindred, Horace, Mapleton, Hunter, Tower City, Enderlin and smaller places such as Alice, Amenia, Ayr and Page.

School districts named for the county include Fargo Public Schools, West Fargo Public Schools, Kindred, Central Cass, Northern Cass, Maple Valley, Enderlin Area, Hope-Page, May-Port CG and Mapleton, which covers only the elementary grades. Some cities sit in more than one district, so one city can have several levies:

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Fargo?
sections.html:
Fargo had 125,990 residents in the 2020 census and covers about 50.8 square miles. It was founded in 1871 and incorporated in 1874. Fargo Public Schools serves most of the city, and West Fargo Public Schools serves the southwestern part.

Large employers include Sanford Health (6,278 full-time equivalent staff), Essentia Health (2,848), West Fargo Public Schools (2,541), North Dakota State University (2,167), Fargo Public Schools (2,064) and the VA Health Care System (1,380). Hector International Airport and the two interstates connect the city.

Cold is part of the house. Fargo's January mean is 9.2 degrees Fahrenheit, July is 70.7, and snowfall averages 51.4 inches a season, with a recorded low of minus 48 and a high of 114.

sections.h2: How does flood history affect a Cass County house sale?
sections.html:
The Red River crested at 39.5 feet in 1997 and 40.84 feet in 2009, and the Fargo area has responded since with sandbagging, infrastructure upgrades, buying houses in flood-prone areas and the FM Diversion project.

For a seller, that history turns into three practical questions:

  • Is the lot in a mapped flood zone, and does the buyer's lender require flood insurance?
  • Has the basement taken water, and is there a sump pump or backup system you should disclose?
  • Did the city or county buy out nearby lots, which could change the street?

Flood facts are not part of your tax bill, but they can affect how a buyer prices the house, so be ready to answer them truthfully.

sections.h2: Who assesses property in Cass County?
sections.html:
The Cass County Tax Equalization office, led by Director Matt Stanger, handles assessment, and the Finance Office bills and collects the tax. The assessor's office is in the Courthouse at 211 9th Street South, Fargo, ND 58103, phone (701) 241-5616. The Finance Office, in the same building, answers at (701) 241-5600.

Assessed value is 50 percent of true and full value, which is market value for residential and commercial property and productivity value for agricultural land. Taxable value is 9 percent of assessed value for residential property and 10 percent for other property. Net consolidated tax adds the taxing entities' mill levies, multiplies by taxable value and subtracts state-paid property tax relief, which the county ties to N.D.C.C. 57-20-07.1.

Cass County also provides a property info site at cass.northdakotaassessors.com and an interactive sales app that shows sales near a parcel. Its exemptions fall into two groups: discretionary ones, such as economic expansion, new home construction or remodeling, and non-discretionary ones, such as government, school, church and park property. It also lists a farm residence exemption, a homestead property tax credit and a disabled veteran credit.

sections.h2: What are the Cass County tax dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Statements are mailed in the first week of December. The first installment of real estate tax is due March 1 and the second October 15. A 5 percent discount comes off the consolidated tax if the full amount is paid by February 15, but it does not apply to specials and drain taxes. When a deadline falls on a weekend or county holiday, it moves to the next business day.

Taxes from prior years accrue interest at 1 percent per month for real estate, added on the first of the month. You can pay online by e-check or card (card use adds a convenience fee), in person at the Finance Office, by mail, or in the secure drop box in front of the Courthouse. The statement carries a parcel number that does not change unless the parcel is split or combined, and a statement number that changes every year.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Cass County assessment?
sections.html:
Cass County describes three steps, and the first is a phone call. Contact the Tax Equalization office at 701-241-5616 to handle concerns informally. Then you can appear before the boards of equalization.

  1. City Board of Equalization, held within the first 15 days of April
  2. County Board of Equalization, held within the first ten days of June
  3. State Board of Equalization, held the second Tuesday of August, which you can reach only if you appeared before both the city and county boards

If you missed the boards, you can file a formal abatement. The county says it must be filed no later than November 1 of the year after the tax becomes delinquent, in duplicate, and physically mailed. The statute is N.D.C.C. 57-23-04, and the form is on the State Tax Commissioner's site.

sections.h2: What happens when Cass County property tax is delinquent?
sections.html:
The Finance Office mails a letter at each stage. Statements of Taxes Owing go to owners with delinquent real estate tax in March, May, July and October. A Notice of Tax Lien goes out in November and explains when interest begins and how foreclosure works. In May, certified mail brings a Notice of Foreclosure of Tax Lien to parcels delinquent for three years, and a $50 fee is added to those parcels.

Mobile homes follow a different path: a Warning and Notice for Delinquent Taxes in August for taxes delinquent one year, then a sheriff's letter about ten business days later, and eventually a sale at the front door of the Courthouse. The county notes that penalty details for mobile homes are on the collector page.

sections.h2: How does a Cass County house sale handle unpaid tax?
sections.html:
The title company pays unpaid property tax from your proceeds at closing. Ask the Finance Office for a payoff that runs through the closing date, because the March, May, July and October steps change the total. Special assessments and drain taxes are shown separately on the statement and also need to be cleared.

Renters make up a large share of Cass County, with about 48.8 percent of occupied homes rented in the 2020 census. That means many sellers are landlords, and a house sold with tenants should come with leases and rent records. We buy Cass County houses as-is, with or without tenants, and we do not quote a price before seeing the property. You owe nothing if you turn our offer down.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Cass County, ND?
faqs.a: Pay the Cass County Finance Office at the Courthouse, 211 9th Street South, Fargo. You can also pay online, by mail or in the drop box in front of the Courthouse.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty in Cass County?
faqs.a: On the first installment and specials, 3 percent after March 1, then 6 percent on May 1, 9 percent on July 1 and 12 percent on October 15. The second installment takes 6 percent after October 15.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for early payment in Cass County?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the full consolidated tax by February 15 earns 5 percent off. It does not apply to special assessments or drain taxes.

faqs.q: When do the Cass County boards of equalization meet?
faqs.a: The city board meets in the first 15 days of April, the county board in the first ten days of June, and the State Board on the second Tuesday of August.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cass County house with delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Request a payoff figure from the Finance Office at (701) 241-5600.
